messages.author: f198db41427babd6
messages.subject: Latent Change model: residual correlations
parts:
Dear lavaan users,

Today I estimated a latent baseline-change, and a latent neighbor change model with the cfa-function in lavaan.

Comparing my results to the corresponding latent state model everything seemed fine (same model fit, latent state intercepts were replicated by the baseline and change intercepts).

In a second step I introduced a manifest predictor (intervention: 0 = control group, 1 = intervention group).

In the baseline change model the correlations between the change-residuals were still estimated but not the correlations between the baseline-residual and the change-residuals.

In the neighbor change model neither the correlations between the change-residuals, nor the correlations between the baseline-residual and the change-residuals were estimated.

Is there a reason for this difference and for the restriction of correlations between the baseline and changes factor residuals?

Thanks a lot!

Elisabeth

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Latent Change model: residual correlations
parts:
I don't think it is safe to assume readers here will be aware of the terms you are using.  Could you post path diagrams of the models you are (a) trying to fit and (b) are actually being fitted by lavaan, highlighting the (un)estimated parameters that are surprising you?

Posting syntax (and data, if available) for a reproducible example also helps to track down problems or suggest changes that enlighten how lavaan works.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.subject: Re: Latent Change model: residual correlations
parts:
Dear Terrence,

Unfortunately I can’t share the data as they are not my own, but I tried to concretize my question with figures, the script, and the output of my baseline and my neighbor change model. As long as I don’t request them explicitly in the model structure I don’t get:

·         The correlations between the state0 (baseline) residuals and the change score residuals (whereas I get the correlations between the change scores) in my baseline model

·         None of these second order residual correlations in my neighbor change model

Is there a special reason why I should not estimate these residual correlations? And is there a reason for the difference between the baseline- and the neighbor-change model?

 

Thanks a lot!

Elisabeth

Am Donnerstag, 2. März 2017 16:35:26 UTC+1 schrieb Elisabeth Zureck:

Dear lavaan users,

Today I estimated a latent baseline-change, and a latent neighbor change model with the cfa-function in lavaan.

Comparing my results to the corresponding latent state model everything seemed fine (same model fit, latent state intercepts were replicated by the baseline and change intercepts).

In a second step I introduced a manifest predictor (intervention: 0 = control group, 1 = intervention group).

In the baseline change model the correlations between the change-residuals were still estimated but not the correlations between the baseline-residual and the change-residuals.

In the neighbor change model neither the correlations between the change-residuals, nor the correlations between the baseline-residual and the change-residuals were estimated.

Is there a reason for this difference and for the restriction of correlations between the baseline and changes factor residuals?

Thanks a lot!

Elisabeth

As long as I don’t request them explicitly in the model structure I don’t get...


From what I understand, lavaan's sem() function will (by default) estimate the correlations among any exogenous factors (which you don't have because only IGCG is exogenous) and any purely endogenous factors (i.e., factors that are outcomes but do not also predict other factors).  You can read descriptions of these defaults in ?lavOptions.  And you can see which variables fall into certain categories using the ?lavNames function to print names of all vs. purely endogenous latent variables.

From your path diagrams and syntax, I can't quite figure out why the first model's output includes estimates of diff10~~diff20, since those are endogenous but also predict stress1 and stress2.  Maybe lavaan also estimates residual covariances between endogenous predictors that are clearly at the "same level" (e.g., like two mediators between X and Y).
Is there a special reason why I should not estimate these residual correlations? And is there a reason for the difference between the baseline- and the neighbor-change model?

I'm not sure, but there are some more LCS-savvy contributors on SEMNET, like Jason Newsom (whose longitudinal SEM book I highly recommend).  Posting that particular question there could result in the advice you seek.
